lena: quick follow-up on the residency-tracking abstraction RFC — i pushed a draft of a slimmer API to the repo, want feedback before I turn it into an RFC
omar: saw it, skimmed. overall +1 to moving telemetry out of the allocator internals. what did you change compared to the draft we discussed last week?
lena: main change is replacing per-op atomic counters with an epoch-sampled aggregator.
lena: goal: keep common path cheap (no atomics on every mark_resident) and still get stable resident_bytes estimates for cost/evict policies
ryan: can you paste the new API sketch here?
lena: sure
lena: ```
// residency.h
struct ResidencyHandle;
ResidencyHandle* residency_register_shard(const char* shard_id, metadata_t meta);
void residency_mark_touch(ResidencyHandle* h, size_t bytes, bool pinned);
ResidencySnapshot residency_snapshot_and_reset(ResidencyHandle* h);
void residency_unregister(ResidencyHandle* h);
```
omar: OK. So mark_touch will just increment a per-thread sample ring and the epoch collector will fold them into totals?
lena: exactly. samples are cheap stores; collector runs on a timer or when there's pressure. avoids churn on hotspots.
maria: worried about correctness for tight latency SLOs — if collector is delayed we might overshoot eviction decisions
lena: good point. plan is hybrid: immediate counters for pinned bytes (small freq) and sampled for transient KV cache pieces
ashley: what about multi-GPU shared allocations? we need consistent shard_id semantics across devices
lena: shard_id is global logical id (model:layer:instance). device-local residency just reports with device tag. aggregation layer normalizes.
ryan: can we get tag dimensions: model_name, seq_len_bucket, evict_policy, device_type? those are useful in console
lena: yes adding those. proposed metrics: resident_bytes, pinned_bytes, resident_objects, residency_hits, eviction_pressure
omar: implementation detail: use relaxed atomics for collector flags, but careful with ABA on unregister
lena: thinking: registration returns a version token; collector checks version before folding; prevents races if unregister happens mid-collect
maria: rollout plan?
lena: can roll out as opt-in via runtime flag per-cluster; enable telemetry-only mode first (no policy change), compare numbers to legacy counters for a week, then flip policy to use new metrics
ashley: perf estimation? overhead added per-touch should be <= 5ns on fast-path
lena: microbenchmarks show ~3.2ns on x86 cores when using per-thread slot write; worst-case collector CPU is negligible unless many shards active
omar: sounds reasonable. one more ask: expose a small debug endpoint to dump per-shard last_snapshot for quick investigation
lena: added to TODO list. will update the draft RFC with API, sampling algorithm, and rollout steps. thanks all :thumbsup:
infra-bot: deploy scheduled: canary telemetry agent will be rolled to infra-canary at 2025-10-07T03:00Z
ryan: nit: add a note about memory accounting for transient prefetched pages (should count as resident until eviction completes)
lena: noted — will add. thanks for the review
maria: thanks!
